# t00A01

## Bundle Overview

- harvested-filename: `apm-t00A01.md`

## Problem Statement

Raw TeX source:

```tex
By an \emph{integral homology $3$-sphere} we mean a closed,
triangulated $3$-manifold $M$ with $H_k(M;\Z)\cong H_k(\Sth;\Z)$ for
all $k\geq 0$. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be integral homology
$3$-spheres. Define $X$ to be the connect sum $M_1\#M_2$ (that is, for
embeddings $\varphi_i:D^3\rightarrow M_i$ for $i=1,2$ of the $3$-disk
$D^3$, form $X$ as the identification space by identifying
$\varphi_1(\partial D^3)$ in $M_1\setminus \varphi_1(D^3)$ with
$\varphi_2(\partial D^3)$ in $M_2\setminus \varphi_2(D^3)$). You may
assume that $\varphi_i(D^3)$ is a $3$-simplex in the triangulation of
$M_i$ ($i=1,2$).
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{alist}
%------------------------------------------------------------------*
\item Compute the fundamental group of $X$ in terms of those of $M_1$
and $M_2$.
%------------------------------------------------------------------*
\item Compute all of the homology groups of $X$. (You do \emph{not}
need to compute the homology groups of $\Sth$.)
%------------------------------------------------------------------*
\end{alist}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

\soln{(Part 2) Though you may need to know what they are in order
to solve the problem.}
```

# t03J01

## Bundle Overview

This directory is the canonical APM problem bundle for this problem.

- informal-solution: `informal-solution.md`
- harvested-filename: `apm-t03J01.md`
- imported-at: `2026-07-13T17:26:57.034041Z`

## Problem Statement

Raw TeX source:

```tex
Let $X$ be a double torus. Let $J_1$ be a curve that cuts $X$ into a
twice-punctured sphere and let $J_2$ be a curve that cuts $X$ into two
once-punctured tori.
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{alist}
%------------------------------------------------------------------*
\item Does $X$ retract to $J_1$? Prove your answer.
%------------------------------------------------------------------*
\item Does $X$ retract to $J_2$? Prove your answer.
%------------------------------------------------------------------*
\end{alist}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

\soln{
(retract: fact: homomorphism induced by inclusion of a retract is injective)  \defn{
\item $(X,t)$ topological space
\item $Y\subset X$ subspace
\item $r:X\rightarrow Y$ retraction
\item $j_*:\pi_1(Y)\rightarrow \pi_1(X)$ homomorphism induced by inclusion
\item $j_*$ injective}
\proof{
\item $r|_Y\circ j$ identity map & retraction:4
\item $y\in Y$ & let
\item $(r|_Y)_*\circ j_*$ identity map of $\pi_1((Y,y))$ & homomorphism induced by identity map is identity map
\item $j_*$ injective & if the identity map factors into two maps, both must be injective}
I don't know if that fact is particularly useful in this case, however, because it seems like each homotopy class in $\pi_1(\Son)$
is going to be mapped to some distinct homotopy class in $\Ttw\#\Ttw$. Well this should be at least true for the curve that cuts $\Ttw\#\Ttw$ into a twice-punctured sphere, since that curve has got to be a generator for the fundamental group of $\Ttw\#\Ttw$. I guess I should work out what exactly the fundamental group of $\Ttw\#\Ttw$ is, that could make things go a bit more easily
(induced homomorphism of fundamental groups) \defn{ % this can be trivially rephrased in terms of pointed topological spaces; they are used anyway.  We can sum up what the induced homomorphism of fundamental groups does as follows: take a representative of the homology class in the first fundamental group, and look at the homology class of the image under the given map of that representative in the second fundamental group.
\item $X$ topological manifold
\item $Y$ topological manifold
\item $h:X\rightarrow Y$ continuous
\item $x_0\in X$
\item $h(x_0)=y_0$
\item $h_*:\pi_1((X,x_0))\rightarrow \pi_1((Y,y_0))$
\item $\forall [f]\in\pi_1((X,x_0)): h_*([f])=[h\circ f]$}
}
```

## Problem Statement

```tex
Without appealing to van Kampen's theorem, prove the following: if
$X=U\cup V$ is a space with $U$ and $V$ are open, path connected and
simply connected, and $U\cap V$ is non-empty and path connected, then
$X$ is simply connected.

\soln{ % somewhat hideously long and all in the Xi style, but it is a proof.
(simply connected: fact: sufficient condition: being the union of two open simply connected subsets whose intersection is path connected; Basic Topology p. 99)  \defn{ % it would be good to have more sufficient conditions for simply connectedness
\item $(X,t)$ topological space
\item $U, V\openset X$
\item $X=U\cup V$
\item $U, V$ simply connected
\item $U\cap V$ path connected
\item $X$ simply connected} 
\proof{ % see also t94A04
\item $x\in U\cap V$ & let % step 1
\item $\alpha:I\rightarrow X$ loop based at $x$ & let % step 2
\item $P:I^n\rightarrow \{0,1\}$ & let % step 3
\item $P(x_1,\ldots ,x_n)=1\Leftrightarrow 0=x_1<\cdots <x_n=1$ & let % step 4
\item $I$ compact metric space & compact metric space: example % step 5
\item inverse images of $U$ and $V$ under $\alpha$ are open & loop is continuous map % step 6
\item inverse images of $U$ and $V$ under $\alpha$ are an open cover of $I$ & every point in $I$ is mapped to a point in $U$ or $V$ % step 7
\item $\{t_0,\ldots ,t_n \in I\}$ & let % step 8
\item $P(t_0,\ldots ,t_n)$ & let  % step 9
\item $\forall k\in \{1,\ldots ,n\}: [t_{k-1},t_k]\subset \alpha^{-1}(U) \vel [t_{k-1},t_k]\subset \alpha^{-1}(V) $ &let (lebesgue's lemma) % step 10
\item $\forall k\in \{1,\ldots ,n\}: \im(\alpha|_{[t_{k-1},t_k]})\subset V \vel \im(\alpha|_{[t_{k-1},t_k]})\subset U$ & step 10% step 9 % step 11
\item $\forall k\in \{1,\ldots ,n\}: \alpha_k:[0,1]\rightarrow X$ & let % step 12
\item $\forall k\in \{1,\ldots ,n\}: \alpha_k(t)=\alpha((t_k-t_{k-1})t+t_{k-1})$ & let % step 13
\item $\alpha_k$ interpolates between the points $\{\alpha(t_k)\}_{k=1}^n$ & step 13 % step 14
\item both $U$ and $V$ are path connected &  simply connected:2  % step 15
\item $\forall k\in \{1,\ldots ,n-1\}: \gamma_k:[0,1]\rightarrow X$ & let % step 16
\item $\gamma_k(0)=x$ & let % step 17
\item $\gamma_k(1)=\alpha(t_k)$ & let ($\alpha(t_k)\in U \vel \alpha(t_k)\in V$; hyp 3, path connectedness)% step 17 % step 18
\item $\alpha(t_k)\in U\Rightarrow \im(\gamma_k)\subset U \et \alpha(t_k)\in V\Rightarrow \im(\gamma_k)\subset V$ & let (path connectedness of $U$ and $V$) % apparently ``simply connected'' implies ``path connected''? yes, it is an explicit hypothesis in the definition! Great.  % step 19
\item $\alpha(t_k)\in U\cap V \Rightarrow$ suitable $\gamma_k$ exists & hyp 4 % step 20
\item $\cdot $ path product & let  % step 21
\item $\gamma_k \cdot \gamma_k^{-1}$ pairs undo each other & $\gamma_k \cdot \gamma_k^{-1}$ can be homotoped to a point % step 22
\item $\alpha\sim \alpha_1\cdot \cdots \cdot \alpha_{n-1}$ & do the paths in order, you traverse same overall path % this should be rigorously cast in terms of the definition of homotopy % step 23
\item $\alpha\sim (\alpha_1 \cdot \gamma_1^{-1})\cdot (\gamma_1 \cdot \alpha_2 \cdot \gamma_2^{-1})\cdot \cdots \cdot (\gamma_{n-1}^{-1}\cdot \alpha_{n-1})$ & steps 22-23 %... undoing what was done before % step 24
\item each of the factors in step 24 is a loop & path product takes loops to loops % step 25
\item the image of each of the factors in step 24 is contained in $U$ or $V$ & steps 11, 13 and 19 % step 26
\item each of the factors in step 24 can be homotoped to a point & step 26; $U$, $V$ simply connected % step 27
\item $X$ simply connected & any loop can be homotoped to a point}
(lebesgue's lemma; Basic Topology p. 49) \defn{ % see Basic Topology item number 3.11
\item $(X,d)$ compact metric space
\item $A$ open cover of $X$
\item $\exists \delta>0:\forall Y\subset X:\diam(Y)<\delta\Rightarrow \exists O\in A:Y\subset  O$}
\proof{ % this is another proof by contradiction. I guess these things are no big deal.
\item $\{Y_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}\subset X$ & let % step 1
\item $\forall i\in \N: \nexists O\in A : Y_i\in O$ & let % step 2
\item $i\rightarrow \infty\Rightarrow \diam(Y_i)\rightarrow 0$ & let (steps 1-3 $\lightning$ concl) % step 3
\item $\forall i\in \N: y_i\in Y_i$ & let % step 4
\item $a\in (y_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ infinitely repeated point or limit point & sequence in compact space contains infinitely repeated point or limit point % step 5
\item $\exists O\in A: a\in O$ & hyp 2 % step 6
\item $\epsilon>0 \et B(a,\epsilon)\subset O$ & let (defn open set)  % step 7
\item $N\in \N \et \diam(Y_N)< \epsilon/2 \et y_N\in B(a,\epsilon/2)$ & let (step 3; step 5 -- choose $N$ so that $y_N$ \emph{is} $a$ or $y_N$ close to $a$) % step 8
\item $d(y_N,a)<\epsilon/2 $ & defn of ball, diameter % step 9
\item $\forall x\in Y_N: d(x,y_N)<\epsilon/2$ & defn of ball, diameter % step 10
\item $\forall x\in Y_N: d(x,a)<\epsilon$ & steps 9-10% step 10 % step 11
\item $Y_N \subset O$ & steps 7, 11 % step 12
\item $\lightning$ & steps 2, 12}
}
```
